prompt:
You describe a timing diagram from an electronics datasheet for an engineer who cannot see it.

Cover, in this order:
1. Every signal, from top to bottom.
2. The sequence of edges and states in time order, and which edge triggers which.
3. Every named interval (for example tSU, tH) with its value and unit, if shown.

Figure type: timing diagram
Section: 5. Host Interface > 5.2 Busy Line Control (LR20xx)
Caption: none
Text inside the figure (exact, from the PDF text layer): BUSY | command processing time | MOSI command
Text that mentions the figure: The BUSY line indicates the status of the chip controller. When the BUSY line is held low, it indicates that the radio is ready to accept a command from the host controller. The BUSY pin is automatically asserted on the falling edge of the NSS. Once the chip has finished processing the command, the BUSY line is de-asserted to indicate that the chip has reached a stable mode device and is ready to accept another command.

Rules:
- When a name or number from "Text inside the figure" is visible in the image, copy it exactly, character for character.
- Never invent a value, name, pin, unit or connection. If something is too small or blurry to read, write "unreadable" instead of guessing.
- Describe only what this image shows. Do not explain general theory or add advice.
- Mention each item once. Stop when everything is covered.
- Plain text only: no Markdown headings, tables or bold. Short paragraphs and "- " lists are fine.
- Start directly with what the figure is (for example "Block diagram of ..."), not with "The image shows".

answer.text:
Timing diagram of Host Interface > 5.2 Busy Line Control (LR20xx).

Signals from top to bottom are MOSI and BUSY.

In time order:
- MOSI starts high, goes low, then high, then low, then high, and remains high during the "command" period.
- BUSY starts high, goes low, and remains low until the end of the "command processing time," after which it goes high.

Named intervals:
- "command" is shown on the MOSI signal.
- "command processing time" is shown between the falling edge of BUSY and the rising edge of BUSY.

Text inside the figure includes: MOSI command, BUSY, command processing time, and command.
